text:
Linger is an open-source personal agent with a Claude-class brain running locally on your PC. 

 
 Open-Source   ·   Local AI   ·   Consumer Macs & PCs 
 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

- A Claude-class brain, running locally. A 125B model on a 12 GB GPU, on everyday Macs and PCs.
- The Grok Bot experience on your PC. Zero token fees for local inference.
- A loyal AI sidekick. It remembers what matters, proactively gets things done, and keeps your data on your device.

 Cool features

 Local models: A Claude-class brain on a 12 GB GPU

 

Efficient AI model–harness co-design brings a full local agent to consumer Macs and PCs. Our MoE inference engine, PolyStrata, keeps a model's busiest experts on your GPU and the rest in RAM or on SSD, so larger models run with less GPU memory: the 125B Qwen3.8-Flash-Next runs on a 12 GB card with 64 GB of RAM. The model runs on your own machine instead of a remote server, so there is no cloud bill and no token fee.

 
 Speed: how fast seven MoE models write on 8, 12 and 32 GB GPUs 

 
 
 Writing, tokens per second 
 Laptop RTX 4070 8 GB 
 RTX 3060 12 GB 
 RTX 5090 32 GB 
 
 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 38.1 (Q2 0)¹ 45.5 179 
 LFM2.5-24B-A2B 70–73 97.8 480–485 
 Flint 40B-A2.5B 61–63 65.5 251–252 
 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 94–100 91.8 394–395 
 Ornith 1.5 76–82 80–82 316–319 
 Gemma 4 26B-A4B 92–93 78.0 (Q4 file) 353–356 
 Tiel Coder 35B-A3B 83 78.8 337–345 
 

¹ Not from PolyStrata's results: our lab measured the Q2 0 file with a short prompt on a 96 GB card held to an 8 GB budget, with 32 GB of RAM and a 64K context. It is not a real 8 GB card, and it does not settle the earlier 95 tok/s IQ1 M figure: Flash-Next Coder IQ1 M gave 32.1 under the same conditions, and the full-model UD-IQ1 M was not tested.

Full results ( 5 more models !) can be found in PolyStrata.

 

 Model Autopilot: The smartest model your machine can run

 

One command detects your hardware, recommends the best model, installs it and checks it. In our lab we run an architecture search: 49 language models, two inference engines, quantizations from 1-bit to 8-bit and context windows from 64K to 256K, tested tier by tier on NVIDIA cards and Macs. On your computer, the installer reads your GPU, memory and bandwidth, keeps only what fits with at least a 64K context, picks the smartest model and then the fastest, and counts it as installed only after it answers a real question.

Not ranked: AIHOT has no third-party results for the model. Test conditions, defaults and self-tests are in Local inference . 

 

 

 Wiki and memory: It remembers your business

 

Tell one agent, and every agent knows. Another Me reads back through your inbox, then each night files your mail, chats and meetings into wiki pages that every agent can search. It keeps the information, preferences and decisions that matter across conversations, on your device instead of in a provider's account.

 
 How it works: your sources become wiki pages every night, and every agent searches them 

 

 

 Proactive Another Me: It speaks up when it matters

 

It reaches out first. Another Me watches your inbox, calendar and Slack, follows up and moves work forward, and messages you only when something needs you. And it improves itself recursively: every night it reads how its own messages landed and rewrites the rules it decides by, so every "not now" makes tomorrow's judgment sharper.

 How it learns: recursive self-improvement, every night

Every message Another Me sends on its own is also a test. Each night, Dreaming reads how those messages landed and rewrites the rules Another Me decides by; the next day it decides with the new rules, and how those land feeds the next night. No retraining: what it learned stays a short list of rules.

 
 Implicit reinforcement: push back on the same kind twice, and it becomes a rule 

You never state the rule; Another Me reads it from how you react. Want it sooner twice, and it tells you right away; turn it down twice, and it stays quiet.

 

 

 

 
 Direct response: say how you want it, and one Dreaming makes it a rule 

No second time needed. Name the kind and it changes whether you are told; name the hour and it changes when.

 

 

 More features

- Desktop and browser: Your apps, your Chrome, already signed in. Agents open the apps on your Mac, Windows PC or Linux desktop and click and type the way you do, and on a Mac or Windows PC they work in your everyday Chrome with the sign-ins you already have.
- Agent teams: One plan for every agent. When a job needs more than one agent, Another Me brings in the agents you have, creates the

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Option 1: the desktop app

For one person on one computer. Choose your platform below. The app opens Linger, connects this computer and runs its agents. Quick Install on its setup screen sets up a Linger server on this computer too.

Platform Package
macOS 14.0 or later, Apple silicon Linger-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg
Windows x64 Linger-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe, or -windows-x64-portable.zip to run without installing
Linux x64 Linger-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz (glibc 2.35 or newer)

There is no package for Intel Macs; use Docker Compose there. Check each download against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release.

See Install the desktop app for the Windows and Linux steps and for help when setup fails.

Option 2: Docker Compose

For a server that several computers share, or to build from source. You need Docker with Compose and at least 5 GiB of memory for its virtual machine.

git clone https://github.com/simplexai-labs/linger.git
cd linger
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build --detach --wait

Create the owner account. As written, it signs in as owner@linger.local with the test password test1234; replace either one to use your own:

printf '%s\n' 'test1234' | docker compose exec -T teamhub \
  teamhub-account create-owner --email owner@linger.local --password-stdin

Change the test password in Settings › Security before other people can reach the server.

Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in. The app then shows the commands that connect your computer. See Install with Docker Compose to serve other computers on your network and to turn on voice.

Local models

The Compose containers run only the Linger server; models and agents run on the computer you connect. On that macOS (Apple silicon) or Linux computer, run the guided installer:

./scripts/install/install.sh

It checks your hardware, installs and verifies a local model after your approval, and connects linger-computer to your Linger server. Run ./scripts/install/install.sh --help for day-2 commands (--status, --up, --remove), or see Bring your own runtime for other model setups.

If Compose ports are busy, the installer offers to select free ports. It saves LiveKit's port mappings and matching RTC startup arguments in .local/compose.ports.yml and enables the override through .env. This requires Docker Compose 2.24.4 or later. Rerunning the installer reuses those ports.
